title: Does System Prompt Framing Affect Sycophancy Recovery Across Model Families?
original_idea: Run identical multi-turn sycophancy correction scenarios on Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Llama 3.1 70B, with and without honesty-enabling system prompts. Compare baseline and prompted correction rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Cross-model sycophancy comparison with prompting interventions has been covered by ELEPHANT and SycEval. ELEPHANT found prompting-based mitigations minimally effective. Limited new insight expected.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: API calls across multiple providers. Straightforward methodology. Slightly more complex than single-model due to multiple APIs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four model families with multi-turn scenarios is broad. API costs and setup for 4 providers plus analysis. Hard to do well in 30hrs.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple 2025-2026 studies have examined sycophancy across model families. ELEPHANT tested 8 models including Claude, GPT-4o, and Llama variants. SycEval (arxiv 2502.08177) evaluated sycophancy across leading models in mathematical and medical domains. Research from PMC (2025) found initial compliance rates approaching 100% across GPT-4o and Llama3-70B. Cross-model sycophancy comparisons with and without system prompt interventions have been partially covered, with ELEPHANT finding that prompting-based mitigations show minimal improvement (3% accuracy gain). The specific combination of multi-turn correction scenarios with honesty prompts across 4 families adds incremental value but the core question has been largely answered.
